page: Microsoft Azure DC48ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCADSv5 family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory configuration provides 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache allocations include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AES, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, and BMI2.

Integrated local storage is bundled with the instance, providing 1933 GB of direct-attached solid-state drive (SSD) capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The machine operates without a dedicated hardware GPU accelerator. Synthetic CPU benchmarks place both single-core (1992.77) and multi-core (49979.86) stress-ng results within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud instances. In-memory data throughput achieves 41.15 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks, representing average tier performance relative to modern hyperscaler offerings.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC48ads_v5 provides dense hardware capacity by bundling substantial local high-speed SSD space directly into the instance allocation, eliminating separate provisioning overhead for scratch disk requirements. A architectural tradeoff is the absence of AVX-512 vector extensions, which limits acceleration for specialized matrix and vector computational routines compared to platforms supporting expanded vector sets.

The hardware profile makes the DC48ads_v5 suitable for relational database engines, Redis caching tiers, ETL pipelines, enterprise application hosting, and distributed compilation workloads where consistent multi-threaded compute and fast local disk access are required.

Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, 192.0 GB of system RAM, and 1933 GB of integrated local SSD storage. It does not include discrete GPU acceleration. The processor includes hardware cryptography extensions like AES and SHA-NI alongside standard AVX vector support, but lacks AVX-512 extensions. Benchmark results show average multi-core and single-core stress-ng throughput alongside 41.15 million Redis SET operations per second. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and bundled high-capacity local storage offer solid density for memory-backed databases, intermediate data staging, ETL pipelines, and general enterprise workloads requiring dedicated multi-threaded compute.
